title: NFAT indicates nucleocytoplasmic damped oscillation via its feedback modulator.
authors: Muramatsu, Masashi; Ito, Takeshi; Shimoji, Hokuto; Komiya, Miko; Miyamura, Yuri; Nishiyama, Koichi; Suzuki, Takashi; Minami, Takashi
one_liner_zh: 该文通过数学模型和实验研究NFAT1与DSCR-1反馈调控的核质振荡，虽涉及转录因子动态调控，但缺乏DNA结合位点预测、互作界面或三维结构建模，且方法为常微分方程模型而非AI或分子模拟，与课题核心匹配度低。
abstract: Cell signaling and the following gene regulation are tightly regulated to keep homeostasis. NF-kappaB is a famous key transcription factor for inflammatory cell regulations that obtain a closed feedback loop with IkappaB. Similarly, we show here, NFAT is also tightly regulated via its downstream target, down syndrome critical region (DSCR)-1. In primary cultured endothelium, either shear stress or VEGF treatment revealed quick NFAT1 nuclear localization following the DSCR-1 transactivation, which in turn induced NFAT1 cytoplasm sequestration. Interestingly, both NFAT and DSCR-1 can be competitive substrates for calcineurin phosphatase and DSCR-1 is known to unstable protein, which caused NFAT1-nucleocytoplasmic damped oscillation via sustained shear stress or VEGF stimulation in endothelial cell (EC)s. To understand the molecular mechanism underlying the NFAT1 oscillation, we built a mathematical model of spatiotemporal regulation of NFAT1 combined with calcineurin and DSCR-1. Theoretically, manipulation of DSCR-1 expression in simulation predicted that DSCR-1 reduction would cause nuclear retention of dephosphorylated NFAT1 and disappearance of NFAT1 oscillation. To confirm this in ECs, DSCR-1 knockdown analysis was performed. DSCR-1 reduction indeed increased dephosphorylated NFAT1 in both the nucleus and cytoplasm, which eventually led to nuclear retention of NFAT1. Taken together, these studies suggest that DSCR-1 is a responsible critical factor for NFAT1 nucleocytoplasmic oscillation in shear stress or VEGF treated ECs. Our mathematical model successfully reproduced the experimental observations of NFAT1 dynamics. Combined mathematical and experimental approaches would provide a quantitative understanding way for the spatiotemporal NFAT1 feedback system.
abstract_zh: 细胞信号传导及随后的基因调控受到严格调控以维持稳态。NF-kappaB是炎症细胞调控中著名的关键转录因子，其与IkappaB形成闭合反馈回路。类似地，我们在此展示，NFAT也通过其下游靶标——唐氏综合征临界区域（DSCR）-1受到严格调控。在原代培养的内皮细胞中，无论是剪切应力还是VEGF处理，均迅速揭示NFAT1核定位，随后伴随DSCR-1反式激活，进而诱导NFAT1细胞质隔离。有趣的是，NFAT和DSCR-1均可作为钙调磷酸酶的竞争性底物，且DSCR-1已知为不稳定蛋白，这导致内皮细胞（EC）在持续剪切应力或VEGF刺激下产生NFAT1核质阻尼振荡。为理解NFAT1振荡的分子机制，我们构建了结合钙调磷酸酶和DSCR-1的NFAT1时空调控数学模型。理论上，模拟中操纵DSCR-1表达预测，DSCR-1减少将导致去磷酸化NFAT1的核滞留及NFAT1振荡消失。为在EC中验证此点，进行了DSCR-1敲低分析。DSCR-1减少确实增加了细胞核和细胞质中去磷酸化NFAT1的水平，最终导致NFAT1核滞留。综合来看，这些研究表明DSCR-1是剪切应力或VEGF处理EC中NFAT1核质振荡的关键责任因子。我们的数学模型成功再现了NFAT1动力学的实验观察结果。数学与实验方法的结合将为NFAT1反馈系统的时空调控提供定量理解途径。
